title: Cascade-free sequences, dispersion index, and state avoidance for stateful digit-wise operations
summary: We show that cascade-free counting from carry theory is a special case of a general transfer matrix construction. For any binary stateful digit-wise operation with GEN/PROP/KILL decomposition, the number of cascade-free sequences of length $L$ depends on only two parameters: the alphabet size $N$ and the product $d = |\text{GEN}| \cdot |\text{PROP}|$. The resulting sequence satisfies $a(L) = N a(L-1) - d a(L-2)$ and equals a scaled Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind with coupling parameter $x = N/(2\sqrt{d}) \geq 1$. We instantiate this for digit-wise addition and doubling in base $p$.…
